title: Foundry IQ knowledge bases
summary: Foundry IQ is a managed, permission-aware knowledge layer. A knowledge base combines knowledge sources with retrieval settings and runs on Azure AI Search agentic retrieval, so several agents can share one governed source of grounding.
useIf: Agents need grounded answers from scattered enterprise content with citations and per-user permissions.
avoidIf: You only need a few ad hoc files in a chat, or one well-tuned index with fixed query logic and a tight latency budget.

explain.md: A Foundry IQ **knowledge base** is a configurable, multi-source resource made of **knowledge sources** (Azure Blob Storage, SharePoint, OneLake, public web) and parameters that control retrieval. Azure AI Search provides the indexing and retrieval underneath, and many agents can share one knowledge base [[r6]]. For indexed sources it can automate chunking, embedding generation and metadata extraction, and schedule recurring indexer runs for incremental refresh [[r6]].

Queries go through **agentic retrieval**: a multi-query pipeline that decomposes a complex question into subqueries, runs them in parallel, semantically reranks results and returns a unified response, optionally using an LLM for query planning [[r6]] [[tr8]]. The knowledge base sets a **retrieval reasoning effort** of minimal, low or medium for that LLM processing [[r6]]. More effort should mean more LLM work and more latency (inference, not a vendor figure).

explain.title: From question to cited answer
explain.alt: An agent asks a knowledge base. Agentic retrieval plans subqueries, searches sources in parallel with the caller identity, reranks, and returns extractive results with citations.

flowchart LR

  KB --> P[Plan subqueries]
  P --> S1[Blob]
  P --> S2[SharePoint]
  P --> S3[OneLake]
  P --> S4[Public web]
  S1 --> R[Rerank and merge]
  S2 --> R
  S3 --> R
  S4 --> R
  R --> A

explain.md: **Permissions.** Foundry IQ synchronizes ACLs for supported sources, honors Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and can run queries under the caller's Entra identity so permissions are enforced at query time [[r6]]. You can use it from Agent Service, Microsoft Agent Framework or any app through the knowledge base REST API or Azure SDKs, and connect it to a Copilot Studio agent [[r6]].

explain.title: Status, checked 2026-10-13
explain.md: Some Foundry IQ features are GA and others preview, depending on the Search REST API version you call. The Foundry and Azure portals continue to provide preview-only access to all agentic retrieval features, and LLM query planning is marked preview in the Search docs [[r6]] [[tr8]]. Foundry IQ is one of three IQ workloads: **Fabric IQ** (semantic layer for analytics in OneLake and Power BI) and **Work IQ** (Microsoft 365 collaboration signals) are the siblings [[r6]].

whereToUse: Enterprise assistants over SharePoint, Blob Storage and OneLake that must respect source permissions
Several agents (prompt, hosted, Agent Framework, Copilot Studio) that need the same governed grounding
Complex questions that benefit from decomposition into subqueries
Answers that need extractive content and citations that trace back to source documents

use: Content is curated, shared across agents and spread over several sources
Permissions matter and you want ACL sync, Purview labels and caller identity enforced
Questions are multi-part and one flat vector query would miss pieces
avoid: A handful of user-provided files in one chat: file search is lighter
A single well-tuned index and a tight latency budget where LLM planning is wasted
Your policy needs every retrieval feature to be GA and the portal path is preview-only
flips: Latency budget tightens: lower the retrieval reasoning effort or query the index directly
Corpus is small and stable: file search or long context can replace a knowledge base
Questions are single-hop lookups: skip LLM planning

pitfalls.symptom: A user sees content from a source they cannot open
pitfalls.cause: The source is not supported for ACL sync, or the query ran under a shared identity
pitfalls.fix: Run queries under the caller's Entra identity and confirm ACL sync support for each source [[r6]].

pitfalls.symptom: Answers are slow on simple questions
pitfalls.cause: LLM query planning and reasoning effort are higher than the question needs
pitfalls.fix: Lower the retrieval reasoning effort to minimal or low and test quality (inference on cost and latency) [[r6]].

pitfalls.symptom: Code that worked in the portal breaks in production
pitfalls.cause: The portal exposes preview-only agentic retrieval features, while the GA surface depends on the Search REST API version
pitfalls.fix: Check the migration guide for what is GA by API version before pinning [[r6]].

scenarios.title: Many sources, per-user permissions
scenarios.situation: A company assistant must answer from SharePoint sites, a Blob container and OneLake data. Each user may see only what their groups allow, and three agents need the same grounding.
unknowns: Are all sources supported for ACL sync?
How fast must a revocation take effect?
scenarios.question: How do you ground the agents?

options.name: One Foundry IQ knowledge base with ACL sync and caller-identity queries
options.why: Shared across agents, permission-aware and built for multi-part questions with citations.
options.tradeoff: Partly preview, LLM planning cost and latency, and revocation depends on ACL sync timing.

options.name: Azure AI Search tool over a custom index with security filters
options.why: Full control of index and filters.
options.tradeoff: You build ingestion, ACL sync and agentic planning yourself.

options.name: File search per agent
options.why: Per-agent vector stores duplicate content and do not enforce source permissions.
options.tradeoff: Right for user-uploaded files in a single chat.

flips.if: Revocation must take effect within seconds
flips.then: Add a live source check on sensitive hits, whatever the retrieval layer.
Build on the GA Search surface and own more of the pipeline.

scenarios.takeaway: Shared, permission-aware grounding is what a knowledge base is for.

scenarios.title: Tight latency, one known index
scenarios.situation: A support widget answers single-hop lookups against one well-tuned search index. The latency budget is tight and questions are short.
unknowns: Does the index already hold ACLs?
scenarios.question: What retrieval do you use?

options.name: Query the existing index directly or with the Azure AI Search tool
options.why: No planning step, and you keep your tuned query logic.
options.tradeoff: No decomposition or managed multi-source features.

options.name: Knowledge base at minimal reasoning effort
options.why: Keeps the managed layer with the least LLM planning.
options.tradeoff: Still extra hops compared with a direct query.

options.name: Knowledge base at medium reasoning effort
options.why: Heavy planning for single-hop lookups spends latency and tokens for little gain.

flips.then: Move to the knowledge base with low or medium effort.
A knowledge base removes custom connector work.

scenarios.takeaway: Do not pay for planning that the question does not need.

quiz.q: Which values does Foundry IQ allow for retrieval reasoning effort?
quiz.explain: The knowledge base page lists minimal, low or medium. The other sets are not Foundry IQ values.

quiz.q: Which permission features does Foundry IQ document?
options: Queries under the caller's Entra identity
Automatic removal of all prompt injection
quiz.explain: The page lists ACL sync, Purview labels and caller-identity queries. It makes no claim to remove prompt injection, which needs separate controls.

quiz.q: Which change most favors dropping a knowledge base for a direct index query?
options: A second agent needs the same content
Questions are single-hop and latency is tight
quiz.explain: Single-hop questions under a tight latency budget do not need LLM planning. The other changes favor a shared knowledge base.

flashcards.front: What is a Foundry IQ knowledge base made of?
flashcards.back: Knowledge sources (Blob, SharePoint, OneLake, public web) plus retrieval settings, run on Azure AI Search agentic retrieval and shareable across agents.
Partly. GA depends on the Search REST API version, while portal access to all agentic retrieval features is preview-only (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: Foundry IQ vs Fabric IQ vs Work IQ?
flashcards.back: Foundry IQ: enterprise knowledge layer. Fabric IQ: semantic layer over OneLake and Power BI. Work IQ: Microsoft 365 collaboration signals.
